# Parser reference corpus

Baseline: OTP-29.1, source commit `751f87b703fe5948607d08e82599ce644b772e76`.
Records were produced with the locally built `build/otp29-install/bin/escript`
(OTP 29.1, macOS arm64). The ignored checkout/install is not a build dependency.

All Erlang examples here are newly authored, small syntax probes. Inspected
upstream tests informed their categories; no upstream test bodies were copied.

| Upstream suite / inspected area | Authored fixture | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stdlib `erl_scan_SUITE`: atoms, numbers, punctuation, strings | literals | scanner and parser |
| stdlib `erl_lint_SUITE`: illegal patterns/guards | lint_only | parses, fails lint |
| compiler `lc_SUITE`: strict generators, multi-template/zip, assignments | comprehensions | parser; feature legality deferred |
| compiler `mc_SUITE`: basic, mixed, multi | comprehensions, maps_records | parser |
| compiler `bs_bincomp_SUITE`: binary generators | comprehensions | parser |
| compiler `bs_match_SUITE`, `bs_construct_SUITE`: segment size/type | binaries | parser; value legality deferred |
| compiler `fun_SUITE`: named/anonymous and references | funs_try_maybe | parser |
| compiler `maybe_SUITE`: conditional match, else | funs_try_maybe | parser |
| compiler `record_SUITE`, `native_record_SUITE`: declarations/access | maps_records, types | parser; resolution deferred |
| `erl_parse` attribute/type builders | attributes, types, bad | parser builders |
| `compile:do_parse_module`, epp | expanded | raw macro syntax fails; expanded syntax succeeds |

`grammar.tsv` inventories every grammar production with its source line, owning
implementation step, AST family, and fixture seed. A seed is not a claim that all
alternatives are already tested; later implementation steps extend its cases.
SSA test productions are explicitly excluded. `builders.tsv` covers ordinary
`build_*` action families. Additional checks such as `check_clauses`, `farity_list`,
`record_fields`, and `attribute_farity` belong to their calling builder's row.

Private records: `.tokens` uses the existing scanner encoding. `.raw` contains
`erl_parse:parse_form` results; `.epp` contains `epp:parse_erl_form` results, including
file attributes; `.lint` independently records lint success/error. AST annotations
normalize to zero; diagnostic line/column coordinates remain. Only file-attribute
paths normalize to basenames. Floats become exact binary64 hex, maps become sorted
key/value pairs, and integers remain arbitrary-size decimal Erlang integers.
Other structure, sequence order, native record identifiers, and literal strings
remain unchanged. Error wording is deliberately excluded. Native expansion traces
are tested separately because OTP annotations cannot represent our full origins.

Offline `parser_reference` checks all native scanner outputs and recorded-file
integrity/classification. `parser_oracle` replays all three reference modes with
the configured installed OTP >=29; native test configuration requires it.
Golden files are never regenerated by CTest. To regenerate, run the oracle with
`raw`, `epp`, or `lint` and an input path;
run the existing preprocessor `scan.escript` for tokens, review the changes, then
update SHA256SUMS. The full upstream Common Test suites have not been executed.

Phase I added `phase1.erl`/`phase1.hrl` and three `.phase1` records for native
AST parity. The private projection now covers all implemented node families;
unknown shapes fail instead of disappearing. The fixture
contains intentional mixed LF/CRLF bytes (protected by `.gitattributes`) and include
dots followed by LF, space, comment, and CRLF. Include return-file line values are
compared exactly. Phase VI adds native/OTP structural comparisons for all original
successful seeds, measured witnesses for all ordinary grammar rows, and a pinned
real-source corpus. See [phase6/README.md](phase6/README.md) for exact scope and
[the host matrix](../../../docs/parser-validation.md) for outstanding validation.
